title: sprint-03: Postgres port of the multi-model forecast, forecast log and verification site (torrance)
goal: Run everything built in sprint 02 on Postgres in Docker (migrations, repeatable loads, same numbers). Beat the published forecast where the data allows it (blend of weather models, recent-bias tracking, an LSTM for days 8-30), keep every forecast in a log, and let the user check any day they observed against what was forecast, on a local site.
pattern: batch ELT: raw -> staging -> marts (Postgres) + per-lead MOS + forecast log + FastAPI site
findings: Daily high, 1-7 days ahead on the test window: the published forecast missed by 1.58 C on average, weatherwise by 1.33 C (-16%). Methods picked in CV, before the test window was used: blend x6, ens_mean x1.
Daily low, 1-7 days ahead on the test window: the published forecast missed by 2.87 C on average, weatherwise by 0.94 C (-67%). Methods picked in CV, before the test window was used: blend x7.
Daily high, 8-30 days ahead: validation picked lstm (validation MAE: decay 2.13, lstm 2.03, mix 2.06). Test-window MAE in C: decay 2.79, lstm 2.87, mix 2.82, climatology 2.85.
Daily low, 8-30 days ahead: validation picked decay (validation MAE: decay 1.15, lstm 1.21, mix 1.17). Test-window MAE in C: decay 2.05, lstm 1.86, mix 1.95, climatology 2.26.
For torrance, Open-Meteo's best_match forecast equals gfs_seamless on 100.0% of rows, so the blend really has three independent weather models, not four.
Published day-ahead max-temp forecasts for torrance (2022-01-01 to 2026-11-13, 1756 days) missed by 1.243 C on average; 20% of days were off by 2 C or more and 8% by 3 C or more (worst 7.4 C).
Forecasts issued 7 days ahead missed by 1.748 C on average; 16% of days were off by 3 C or more.
Bias: published max temps run -0.62 C at lead 1 over the whole period (positive = forecast too warm); it drifts by year as the upstream model changes.

Test window (2025-11-14 onward), max temp: a correction was chosen in CV at every lead; correction lowered error at lead 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7; no lead got worse. The p10-p90 range held the actual value on 72.9% to 78.4% of days (target 80%).

min temp: a correction was chosen in CV at every lead; correction lowered error at lead 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7; no lead got worse. The p10-p90 range held the actual value on 72.9% to 79.7% of days (target 80%).
Beyond a week: max temp lead 30: model 2.91 C vs climatology 2.86 C vs persistence 4.09 C; min temp lead 30: model 2.1 C vs climatology 2.3 C vs persistence 2.45 C.

limits: Actuals are ERA5 reanalysis for the grid cell, not a weather station; the last few days of the archive are preliminary.
Published forecasts are Open-Meteo's best-match model (previous_dayN hourly values aggregated to daily max/min), not a specific app's forecast.
Leads 8-30 have no day-level skill in any public model; the 30-day line is a seasonal expectation with a measured range, not a weather forecast.
One test window of 12 months; MAE differences under about 0.1 C are within noise.
Training rows are cut on target date, not issue date: up to 6 days of actuals just before the test window were not yet known when a lead-7 forecast was issued (about 0.1% of rows).
Temperature only. Rain is fetched but not modelled this sprint.

The site compares your reading with a forecast of the grid-cell value. A yard thermometer or a nearby airport can sit a steady 1-3 C away from the grid data; the scoreboard reports that gap separately.
Method list revised once after seeing sprint-02 test numbers (adaptive range and the mix candidate were added then). The clean check from here on is the live forecast log against entries on the site.
Recent-bias and adaptive-range inputs assume yesterday's actual is in the archive when today's forecast is made; the newest archive days are preliminary.
A forecast issued during the day is up to a day fresher than the lead it is scored as (previous_dayN means at least N x 24 hours old).
